description_en: The province's main public art museum, a low concrete building with a reflecting pool set in green foothills on the road toward Hallasan. It shows Jeju and Korean modern art plus changing special exhibitions, and has a hall for painter Chang Ri-suok's donated works.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticketing ends 30 min before close); Jul-Sep 09:00-20:00. Temporary: during 2026 Jeju Biennale (Aug 25-Nov 15, 2026) 10:00-18:00 from Oct 1.
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public holiday, the next non-holiday weekday); Jan 1; Seollal; Chuseok
admission_note: Official site (fetched 2026-11-11): adult 25-64 8,000 / youth 13-24 4,000 / child 7-12 2,000 KRW; 50% off for Jeju residents and groups of 10+; free for age 6 and under. KTO/VisitJeju still list adult 2,000 KRW. Free entry Nov 3-15 (Biennale) and Nov 16-Dec 7, 2026 (exhibition changeover).
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
terrain: flat indoor galleries; paved/lawn forecourt with outdoor sculptures
notes: FEE CONFLICT: the official museum fee page lists adult 8,000 KRW, with no effective date; KTO (TourAPI), access.visitkorea, VisitJeju and MCST exhibition listings all say 2,000 KRW. I could not find a news report of a fee increase, so I used the official figure; recheck it. KTO accessibility listing says there are no steps at the entrance and no indoor level changes, plus an elevator, free wheelchair and stroller rental, accessible parking and a nursing room. It says 'restroom available' but does not say whether it is accessible. has_stairs=false is about the visitor route only, based on that listing. Delmoondo cafe on site. avg_stay_min is an estimate. Jibun in the 2015 data (연동 680-7) differs from the current road address; the road address above is the one all current sources use.

description_en: A shallow, calm white-sand beach with emerald water on Jeju's northeast coast, about 20 km east of the airport, backed by a lawn park and the green Seoubong hill. A paved seaside promenade and a small arched footbridge make it easy to stroll, and Seoubong's coastal trail is popular at sunset.
opening_hours: 24h / always open. 2026 swimming season Jun 24-Sep 6, swimming 10:00-19:00 (no night swimming in 2026).
admission_note: Free beach access. In season, parasol rental 20,000 KRW and raised platform (평상) 30,000 KRW.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
terrain: sand beach; narrow paved/deck seaside promenade; arched footbridge (~11 deg); optional Seoubong cement/dirt path with slopes
notes: ADDRESS CONFLICT: VisitJeju and Wheelnavi give 조함해안로 525 (jibun 함덕리 1004-10); KTO and access.visitkorea give 조함해안로 519-10. I used 525. Wheelnavi (Jeju barrier-free tourism site) lists accessible parking, separate men's and women's accessible restrooms, and pergola/pavilion rest spots, and says there is no assistive-device rental. Its warnings: the promenade is narrow and has drain covers; the lawn plaza and the end of the Seoubong path are reached by stairs; there is a 5-9 deg downhill from the parking lot. No beach wheelchair or mat is documented. Accessible parking is at the control-center lot. A visitor review on VisitJeju says there are no showers, only taps; this is unofficial. The east end has a dog-swim zone in summer. avg_stay_min is an estimate; add 40-60 min if climbing Seoubong (an oreum).

name_en: Jeju 4·3 Peace Park (Jeju 4·3 Peace Memorial Hall)
description_en: A large memorial park and museum on the lower slopes east of Jeju City that remembers the tens of thousands of civilians killed during the Jeju April 3rd Incident (1947-1954). The memorial hall tells the history through six themed galleries with multilingual commentary, while the grounds hold the memorial altar, victims' name stones, and burial-site monuments.
opening_hours: Outdoor park: 24h / always open. Memorial Hall: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00).
closed_days: Park: none. Memorial Hall: 1st and 3rd Monday of each month (if a public/substitute holiday, the next non-holiday day).
admission_note: Free admission to park and memorial hall; free parking.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
terrain: mostly flat paved paths with some unpaved sections; ~330 m gentle uphill (3-5 deg) to memorial tower; ramps beside steps at altar/plaza
notes: access.visitkorea lists a ramp entrance to the hall, an elevator, wheelchair rental, stroller rental at the info desk and 2 accessible parking spaces. It says 'restroom available' but not whether it is accessible. Accessible restrooms are confirmed by Wheelnavi (separate men's and women's) and by Dooritogether/jejudoori (1F and 2F of the hall, plus outside the Peace Education Center). An older KTO listing marked accessible facilities as absent; it looks outdated. Wheelchair users are advised to bring a companion because of the 330 m slope and some unpaved stretches. Accessible parking is in parking lot 3 (jejudoori). Multilingual commentary videos are available (KO/EN/ZH/JA/KSL). Wheelnavi lists a cafe. Seating/benches were not confirmed. The hall is a 4-storey building plus basement. This is an emotionally heavy topic. avg_stay_min is an estimate (hall about 60-90 min plus grounds).

description_en: A cool, shady forest of tall Japanese cedars on the lower slopes east of Jeju City, laced with gentle deck and mat-covered walking paths, a mineral spring and a pond. A steeper side trail climbs Jeolmul Oreum for views toward the sea.
admission_note: Adult 1,000 / youth 600 / child 300 KRW (groups of 20+ discounted). Free for age 6 and under, 65+, people with disabilities and some other groups. Parking extra (compact 1,500, mid/small 3,000, large 5,000 KRW).
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI / 대한민국 구석구석 관광정보 사진) - photographer and KOGL type not shown
terrain: gentle forest deck paths and coir-mat (야자매트) trails, no steps on main routes; optional oreum trail is steeper
notes: HOURS CONFLICT: KTO and access.visitkorea give the seasonal 07-18 / 07-17 hours; VisitJeju lists entry 07:00-17:00 year-round. Today (Nov) both agree on 07:00-17:00. Fees come from KTO/ktriptips; the foresttrip official page does not list them. Parking fees come from a third-party listing. access.visitkorea lists 3 accessible parking spaces, an accessible restroom, 3 manual wheelchairs and 4 strollers to borrow (ask at the ticket office), and a deck/ramp main route through the cedars that is easy by wheelchair. has_stairs=false applies to the main walking routes only; the Jeolmul Oreum climb is a separate, steeper trail. wheelchair_ok is 'partial' because only the deck routes are suitable. has_seating=true is based on benches visible at the entrance in the KTO photo. The source data's '국립' label: the land is Korea Forest Service national forest, but on-site operation is by Jeju City's 절물생태관리소. The jibun (봉개동 산 78-1) matches VisitJeju. Some trails were closed for maintenance Mar-Jun 2026 and have reopened (Jul 2026 news). avg_stay_min is an estimate.

description_en: A cluster of eight thatched-roof buildings near Jeju Port recreating the merchant inn run by Kim Man-deok, an 18th-century Jeju businesswoman remembered for using her fortune to feed islanders during a famine. Some buildings hold a small free exhibit on old Jeju life; the others work as a traditional tavern serving local dishes. The Kim Man-deok Memorial Hall is a short walk away.
closed_days: Mon (VisitJeju; weekly vs alternate-week Mondays conflicting)
admission_note: Viewing buildings are free; the tavern (주막) sells food (e.g., bracken haejangguk about 10,000 KRW per an Apr 2026 blog). Nearby Kim Man-deok Memorial Hall (산지로 7) is also free.
terrain: small courtyard with level changes; slopes up to ~13 deg to the tavern building
notes: Opening hours not confirmed from an official source. A search summary of EasyJeju data (surveyed 2023) gave 11:00-22:00 (last order 21:00), closed Mon. Trazy gives 10:00-21:00 daily. Both are unverified, so opening_hours is null. VisitJeju contradicts itself: its metadata says alternate Mondays closed, its text says every Monday. Jibun: VisitJeju gives 건입동 984-41 (EasyJeju 984-56), which differs from the 2015 data (1292). Run by the Geonip-dong village cooperative. Accessibility comes from EasyJeju (Jeju Tourist Accessibility Center), surveyed 2023-06-09: no accessible parking or accessible restroom; 11 cm step at the viewing-hall entrance; slopes up to 13 deg; stairs in the indoor table area; and an obstacle at the tavern entrance that makes wheelchair use difficult. Whether there is a general restroom is not confirmed. Pets allowed per VisitJeju tags. Thatched-house photo checked visually. It is a .webp file from the VisitJeju CDN (returns HTTP 200, image/webp); the KTO set for this area shows only the memorial hall. NEARBY Kim Man-deok Memorial Hall (김만덕기념관): 산지로 7, 064-759-6090, www.mandukmuseum.or.kr, 09:00-18:00, closed Mon (next weekday if Mon is a holiday), Jan 1, and Seollal and Chuseok days; free; Korean guided tours, audio guide in KO/EN/ZH/JA/Jeju dialect; VisitJeju says wheelchair and stroller rental is available and tags it barrier-free. KTO image of the hall: https://tong.visitkorea.or.kr/cms/resource/12/4129912_image2_1.jpg. avg_stay_min is an estimate (about 40 min for the inn alone, about 90 min including the memorial hall or a meal).
